analyst_view.overall: Early view: a bottom-half clash between Le Havre (18th, winless, 2 points) and a Strasbourg side whose coach Hugo Oliveira, one report says, is under strong pressure after five defeats in six. Le Havre's bench (Didier Digard suspended, academy director Jair Karam in interim charge) may have changed by then, and both clubs have conceded 22 goals.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean higher: both defences have conceded 22 in 10 games, and Le Havre let in three or more in three straight league games before the 0-2 against Lorient. Strasbourg also score 1.8 a game, so this has the look of an open game.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.2 corners. I lean lower: Strasbourg win the fewest corners in the league (2.5 a game) and had one at Toulouse. Le Havre average 5.3, so most corners will come from the home side.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean higher: it is a relegation-zone match between two teams on poor runs, and Le Havre are 5th for fouls (14 a game). Strasbourg got three yellows in their last game at Toulouse.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots. I lean slightly higher: Le Havre average 16.1 shots a game (4th) and Strasbourg 12.6, and both defences give up a lot. A home side that has to win will keep shooting.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. Season figures (Le Havre 5.0, Strasbourg 4.9 a game) support that, so I stay with it. Le Havre's finishing has been poor, which balances their volume.
